tone.quote: Если за долгим слогом следует другой долгий ударный слог, то первый укорачивается. Это правило широко распространено в КАД: bÎt/bit×. В этом случае долгий Î > i. Подобное явление характерно и для других арабских диалектов. Два долгих слога в слове в КАД почти не встречаются. Безударный долгий слог укорачивается, а ударный сохраняет долготу: gÁlÁ > galÁ – "сказал ему". Это явление не нарушает фонологической структуры слов, т.к. в КАД долгота и краткость гласных не создаёт фонологических оппозиций. [...] В КАД в таджикских заимствованиях ударение, в основном, падает на последний слог.
tone.locator: Part I 'Фонетика-фонология', section 'Система гласных', p. 23; loanword remark in the text commentary, p. 198
tone.translation: If a long syllable is followed by another long stressed syllable, the first one shortens. This rule is widespread in QAD: bīt/bitī. In this case long ī > i. A similar phenomenon is characteristic of other Arabic dialects too. Two long syllables in one word hardly ever occur in QAD. An unstressed long syllable shortens, while a stressed one keeps its length: gālā > galā 'he said to him'. This does not disturb the phonological structure of words, since in QAD vowel length and shortness create no phonological oppositions. [...] In QAD, stress in Tajik loanwords mostly falls on the last syllable.
tone.summary: No tone described; only stress-length interaction (pretonic long-vowel shortening) and final stress in Tajik loans; intonational 'stress' with high rise is phrase-level.

tone.quote: The identified 5 cardinal phonological units do not distinguish phonological length. This phenomenon should be considered as a characteristic feature of the QAD vowel system. Occurrence of long vowels in words should be ascribed to various factors. The most important of these, in the present writer’s view, is stress. [...] Stress Stress is not fixed in the QAD. It falls manly on long syllables. If the word contains two long syllables, postposition is given preference. birgÁdÙr “team-leader” ilbÁsÇt “clothes”
tone.locator: English summary, section 'Phonology' > 'Stress', p. 241 (vowel-length sentences p. 240)
tone.summary: No tone system described (Arabic dialect; prosody treated only as word stress: free, weight-driven, rightmost long syllable).
